title: SearchResponse
description: POST /v1/ask 200 body (public: /search/v1/ask). Canonical shape: search/app/server.py (class SearchResponse). EXTENSIBLE: additionalProperties is deliberately open (2026-08-13) — the server may add fields, and a client MUST ignore ones it does not know. Adding a field is therefore never a breaking change; removing or retyping one is. The request schema stays closed, so a misspelled request field is still an error.

answer.description: Curated (QA), generated (RAG), or guard message. May be empty when outcome=suggest. FORMAT: plain text with one markdown feature — **bold** — used for the paragraph lead-in when the answer spans several documents ("**Jednotné testy:** …"). A client that renders the string verbatim shows the asterisks, so it must either convert **…** to bold or strip the markers; no other markdown is emitted.

outcome.description: What kind of result this is. 'blocked'/'self_harm'/'unusable' come from the guard; 'no_answer' means nothing cleared the gates; 'role_required' (init 127) means the caller sent no usable role and none of the corpus is visible without one — the answer field carries the localized ask, render it like any other answer; 'llm_unavailable' (init 139) means the ANSWER MODEL failed, not the corpus — never tell the user to rephrase, and on the streaming endpoint the answer field may hold the partial text that was already streamed followed by the notice.

answer_source.description: Coarse origin of the answer. Finer than this: `strategies`. 'meta' covers both deterministic answers the route guard gives about the assistant or the school itself, without retrieval or an LLM call: the capabilities answer ("co umíš?"), built from the corpus's own headings, and since 2026-09-18 the school-identity answer ("jak se jmenuje naše škola?"), read from legal_entity.display_name. The enum is deliberately unchanged — the two are told apart in flow_trace, where trace_detail.guard is 'meta' or 'identity'.

strategies.description: Granular retrieval steps that contributed, in order (e.g. ['document_lexical'] or ['qa_lexical']). Populated by the executor.

suggestions.description: ALWAYS present. What the user could ask next; how (and whether) to render it is entirely the client's decision. THE CONTRACT: every item's `question` (and every string in `options`) is a text that can be sent straight back to /v1/ask as the next question — render, tap, resend, no other semantics needed. Populated on every outcome except the guards (blocked/self_harm/unusable, which deliberately offer nothing). An exact QA hit carries RELATED curated questions (there is nothing to disambiguate, but there is something to ask next); before 2026-09-03 it offered nothing. May still be empty when the system genuinely has nothing to offer (e.g. an empty corpus).

kind.description: qa = a curated question ('did you mean?' next to a suggest/no_answer, or a related curated question next to a QA answer). clarify = the retrieved documents span different domains; `question` is the clarifying sentence to show and `options` are the ready-to-send refinements — the answer is still generated, the chat decides whether to show it or ask first. related = a section of an answering document that was retrieved but did not fit the context. variant = an LLM rephrasing of the question, offered when the retrieval pool came back empty. other_grade = a curated question that exists for a DIFFERENT ročník than the caller's. variant and other_grade were emitted in production but missing from this enum until 2026-08-21, so a client generated from this schema rejected real responses. Every kind here keeps the contract that `question` can be sent straight back — clarify is the sole exception, and it is off by default (platform_setting suggest_clarify).

question.description: kind=qa: the entry's canonical_q. kind=clarify: the localized clarifying sentence (system_message 'clarify_domains'). kind=related: the section heading (headings are their own search signal, so it works as a query).

score.description: 0..1 relevance of the entry (coverage or trigram similarity). kind=qa only.

label.description: What to SHOW: the domain's display name from document_type_taxonomy in the query's language.

question.description: What to SEND: the best section heading of that domain's document. A heading is its own retrieval signal, so resent as a query it lands in its document — appending the display label to the original question instead was measured to dilute the query into no_answer.

options.description: kind=clarify only: one option per domain found in the answer. Render `label`, send `question`.

file_uuid.description: kind=related only: the document the section belongs to.

matched_entry_id.description: qa_entries.entry_id of the winning/closest curated entry (QA branches only).

match_score.description: 0..1 relevance of the winning/closest result; the metric depends on the retrieval method. QA lexical & RAG lexical/keywords: content coverage. QA vector & RAG vector: cosine. QA exact: 1.0. Null on guard/no_answer. Disambiguated by the query log's strategies_text.

key_words_used.description: Query concepts the keyword step matched (union of keyword_match over the chunks it returned). Empty on every other path: a QA hit or a purely lexical/vector answer used no keywords.

delivered_by.description: Always 'online' from this service. The constant exists so a client that can also answer from an on-device library tags both kinds of turn the same way.

effective_scope.description: What the search ACTUALLY ran with — škola, role, ročník. NOT the spec's memberships[] with an `applied` flag: that presumes a token the server can enumerate memberships from, and this service has none (entity, role and ročník arrive per request).

role.description: code_list('role') code as validated. Null when the request carried none and the policy allows it — or on outcome=role_required, where null IS the finding.

school_grade.description: The ročník the cascade USED — may be derived from the question text when the request sent none.

language.description: Language filter that restricted retrieval; null = no restriction.

domains.description: The THEMATIC AREAS the search was restricted to, canonical (trimmed, upper-cased, deduplicated, sorted) — or null for no restriction. Codes, never the internal taxonomy_rules ids: those are per-entity and no client has a use for them. ONLY EVER A VALIDATED VALUE, including on the early return outcome=role_required, where the domain resolver has deliberately already run — a response never presents an unchecked filter as the one that applied. A client compares this with what it selected to detect that its stored choice no longer matches. Additive: a response from before this field existed simply omits it, which reads as no restriction.

identified.description: Whether the caller was identified. The private branch of the visibility predicate depends on it, so it answers 'why do I not see my own document'.

sources.description: Source documents (see rag-source.schema.json). Populated on outcome=answer from RAG (documents actually retrieved) and, since 2026-08-24, from QA (the sources the curator cited in the pack's `sources` column — no file_uuid on those, only rank/title/url). Empty on every other outcome. A client MUST NOT infer the answer's origin from this array being non-empty — that is what answer_source is for. Was a JSON STRING until 2026-08-13 — clients no longer parse it a second time.

language.description: ISO 639-1 answer language. Currently always 'cs' on the deterministic paths; the RAG answer follows the question language (prompt rule, not enforced).

duration_ms.description: Server-measured wall time for the cascade, milliseconds.

answer_parts.description: The same answer split per paragraph, each carrying the document it came from. A multi-document answer is written as one paragraph per document, so a client can render each next to a link to its source instead of parsing the markdown. `answer` still holds the whole text — this is additive. Empty for QA and guard answers.

index.description: 0-based paragraph order. Deliberately NOT the same base as source_rank / sources[].rank, which are 1-based — index is only this array's position and is never an offset into sources; the published contract shows 0 and clients were written against it.

lead_in.description: Topic label the paragraph opens with, markers stripped.

markdown.description: The paragraph as generated, lead-in still **bold**.

source_rank.description: Rank in `sources`; null when the paragraph could not be attributed with certainty — a wrong link is worse than none.

excerpt.description: The source text this paragraph was written from: the chunks of that document which were in the context, in reading order, each introduced by its heading. Meant for a "show the source" affordance next to the link. null when the `include_excerpt` parameter is off or the paragraph is unattributed; cut at `excerpt_max_chars` and marked with […].

trace.description: Per-step cascade trace: EVERY configured step in order with what it did (ran/skipped/disabled/error), its timing, what it added to the chunk pool and which step ended the walk. ALWAYS present — the server sends it on every response, so a client validating against this schema needs it declared even though it is diagnostic and the mobile client ignores it. Its inner shape is deliberately unconstrained: it is a debugging surface, not a contract.
